body:
The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) has invested US$50 million in a climate fund overseen by US alternative manager TPG Inc to support climate finance across Asia, the Middle East and Africa.

AIIB will also commit up to a further $50 million in co-investment to boost climate investment through the TPG Rise Climate Global South Initiative Fund, the bank says in a statement on October 14.

“Through this partnership with TPG, AIIB is supporting the expansion of innovative climate solutions in emerging markets, while strengthening climate finance ecosystems across our members,” says Kim-See Lim, chief investment officer for the regional public sector and global financial institutions and funds clients at AIIB, in the statement.

Lim adds that the investment aligns with the bank’s target of directing 50% of its annual financing to private-sector-oriented operations by 2030.

Launched in September 2024, the fund is designed to target investments in sectors including energy transition, green mobility, sustainable fuels, sustainable materials and products, carbon solutions, climate adaption and resilience.

The fund is anchored by a US$500 million commitment from Alterra Management, a climate investment vehicle funded by the government of the United Arab Emirates.

Beijing-based AIIB is a multinational development bank with 106 member countries.
